# Closing Brackets

> Closing Brackets is an AI-native web agency. Build-a-Bot is a custom agent
> that handles the tasks you delegate. We build the site or app a business
> runs on, and on that same property we hire one custom agent to take a
> defined set of delegated tasks. The client stays the manager. Every
> engagement is one written scope, a timeline with real dates, and one fixed
> price — there is no hourly billing, and the client owns the code.

Founded and run by Robert Campbell (robert@closingbrackets.com). Based in
Spokane, Washington (Inland Northwest), remote-capable, serving clients in the
United States. A builder-led studio: the person who scopes the work writes the
code and is still there when it goes live.

## What we do

- [Build-a-Bot](https://closingbrackets.com/build-a-bot/): A custom agent for the tasks you delegate — lead qualification and booking, review responses, recall and reactivation, inbox triage, document intake and extraction, quote follow-up, invoice and AP assist, drafted content queued for a human. Scoped by one job letter (tasks in, tasks out), wired to the tools the client already uses, with a stop condition and a named human it escalates to. Not a chatbot, not a platform, not unlimited agents.
- [Web & app](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#web-app): Professional sites, storefronts, customer portals and custom apps, built A to Z. Working software at every milestone; the client owns all of the code.
- [Engineering bar](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#engineering-bar): Performance, accessibility, security and SEO foundations — part of every build, or a standalone audit.
- [SEO & growth](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#seo-growth): Search, local presence and conversion work on the property.
- [AI consulting](https://closingbrackets.com/services/#ai-consulting): Where a bot pays off in a business and where it does not; usually becomes a job letter rather than a strategy deck.

## Three engagement shapes

1. Property only — a site or app. A bot is never forced.
2. Build-a-Bot only — an agent hired onto systems the client already has.
3. Property + bot — the default AI-native package: the site or app is the front door, the agent works behind it.

## How Build-a-Bot works

- The scope is a job letter: what the client delegates, and what they do not. If it is not in the letter, it is not in the bot. More tasks = a change order or a second bot.
- The agent will not make pricing exceptions or refunds without a written rule, will not give clinical, legal or financial sign-off, and will not run without a stop condition and an escalation name.
- Starting price bands (exact price comes from the job letter): one delegated job on existing systems from $6,000; two or three related jobs, or messy wiring, from $12,000; optional oversight after day 30 from $1,500 per month. No hourly billing.
- Typically 21 days from signed letter to production agent, plus 30 days of stabilising included.
- Process for every project: scope → build → integrate → hand over → stabilise.

## How engagements work

- Fixed scope: one document says what gets built. If it is not in there, it is not in the price.
- Real dates: a timeline with actual dates, not a range that slides.
- One price: a single fixed price agreed before anything starts. No hourly billing, no time and materials.
- The client owns all code, configuration and data. Nothing is locked to a retainer for handover.
- A fit if the owner can name work they already wish someone would take. Not a fit for a homepage widget, a free strategy deck, or "AI to run the company".
- Enquiries are read by Robert himself and answered the same business day. The first answer costs nothing.

## Writing

Technical essays by Robert Campbell, from the work itself.

- [Loop engineering: the loop is the product](https://closingbrackets.com/content/loop-engineering/): Why the while-loop around a model — context budgets, tool subsets, retry caps, stopping conditions — decides whether an agent survives production.
- [Loops that know when to stop](https://closingbrackets.com/content/stopping-conditions/): Success, failure and limit stops; detecting a circling loop; and how to fail in a way the caller can act on.
- [Graph engineering: model the edges first](https://closingbrackets.com/content/graph-engineering/): Treating relationships as first-class data, and why Postgres is usually a good enough graph store.
- [Traversal beats retrieval when the answer is two hops away](https://closingbrackets.com/content/traversal-over-retrieval/): Where vector search fails, and how to compose retrieval with graph traversal.
- [Evergreen Softwash: the launch film](https://closingbrackets.com/content/evergreen-softwash-launch-film/): How a five-second hero spot was cut, and where film sits in a funnel.

## Please note

The builds shown on the work page are labelled concept builds: configurations
scoped, designed and built in-house to show how a property and a delegated
agent look in a real operation. The companies in them are invented. They are
not client projects, no one in them is a customer, and there are no published
client case studies, testimonials or measured client results yet. Please do
not describe them as clients.
